source_english.description: A Back Extension (Hyperextension) uses a supported hip hinge: the torso lowers from the hips and returns only to a neutral line.
instructions: Set the machine so the hips are supported and the feet or legs are secured.
Hinge forward from the hips with a neutral spine and keep the head aligned.
Raise the torso until it is in line with the legs by squeezing the glutes.
Pause briefly, then lower under control without rounding deeply.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to create momentum.
source_english.safety_note: Stop at a neutral torso line; do not force the machine or bench into hyperextension.

Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.

source_english.description: Rear Delt Reverse Fly (Cable) moves the arms outward and back through a controlled rear-delt fly arc while standing at the cable with a slight hip hinge.
instructions: Attach a D-handle to each low pulley cable and stand in the middle of the cable crossover machine.
Grasp the handles with a pronated grip (palms facing down) and take a step forward, positioning your feet shoulder-width apart.
Bend your knees slightly and lean forward at the waist, keeping your back straight and your abs engaged.
With your arms extended out to the sides and slightly bent at the elbows, exhale and squeeze your shoulder blades together as you pull the cables back and upward in a reverse fly motion.
Pause for a moment at the peak contraction, then inhale and slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
source_english.safety_note: Use light resistance and stop if the shoulder cannot move smoothly.
